question: GQ-001
subject: a half-built index was indistinguishable from a healthy one
the_risk_i_noted_and_left: last turn I wrote that the rebuild now exceeds a ten-minute foreground call. I did not ask what a killed rebuild leaves behind.

measured.simulation: deleted rows to mimic a rebuild dying at book 300
measured.result: an index of 300 books against 673 texts on disk
measured.why: build-external-passages REMOVES the index file before writing, so a death mid-run leaves a plausible, smaller, entirely silent result

fix: --check now compares the index against the source texts on disk

the_distinction_that_makes_it_usable.problem: a fetch in flight adds texts the index has not seen — normal and self-correcting
the_distinction_that_makes_it_usable.solution: look twice. If the text count is still moving, report STALE and exit 0; if it is static, report INCOMPLETE and exit 8
the_distinction_that_makes_it_usable.measured: 677 then 678 twenty seconds apart during a live fetch

proven_both_ways.fixture_truncated_no_fetch: INCOMPLETE: 2 books but 6 texts and the count is not moving — exit 8

and_the_same_defect_again.what: my first fixture test read the REAL vault — 684 texts instead of the 6 in the fixture
and_the_same_defect_again.cause: rebuild-corpus.sh hardcoded DB, the exact defect I fixed in seven .mjs builders — sitting in the pipeline that runs them
and_the_same_defect_again.fix: the pipeline now honours VAULT_ROOT and CORPUS_DB
and_the_same_defect_again.count: fourth time this session a probe read the real thing instead of the fixture
